etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Late Middle English solar, from Latin sōlāris, from sōl (“sun”), from Proto-Indo-European *sóh₂wl̥ (“sun”).

definitions.definition: Of or pertaining to the sun; proceeding from the sun
(astrology, obsolete) Born under the predominant influence of the sun.

quote.citation: 1700, [John] Dryden, “The Cock and the Fox: Or, The Tale of the Nun’s Priest, from Chaucer”, in Fables Ancient and Modern; […], London:  […]  Jacob Tonson, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: and proud beside, as solar people are

definitions.definition: Measured by the progress or revolution of the sun in the ecliptic; as, the solar year.
Produced by the action of the sun, or peculiarly affected by its influence.

quote.citation: 1627 (indicated as 1626), Francis [Bacon], “(please specify the page, or |century=I to X)”, in Sylua Syluarum: Or A Naturall Historie. In Ten Centuries. […], London:  […]  William Rawley […]; [p]rinted by J[ohn] H[aviland] for William Lee […], →OCLC:
quote.text: They denominate some herbs solar, and some lunar.

quote.citation: 2013 July 20, “Out of the gloom”, in The Economist, volume 408, number 8845:
quote.text: Nor is solar power yet as cheap as the grid.

quote.citation: December 13 2021, Molly Ball, Jeffrey Kluger, Alejandro de la Garza, “Elon Musk: Person of the Year 2021”, in Time Magazine‎[1]:
quote.text: He’s a player in robots and solar, cryptocurrency and climate, brain-computer implants to stave off the menace of artificial intelligence and underground tunnels to move people and freight at super speeds.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English solar, soler; from a conflation of Old English soler, solere (“raised platform; loft, upper room, upper part of a house, soler”), from Latin sōlārium; and Old English solor, salor (“residence, dwelling; hall; palace”), from Proto-West Germanic *salaʀ, from Proto-Germanic *salaz, *salą (“house, room, hall”). More at sale.

definitions.definition: (obsolete) A loft or upper chamber forming the private accommodation of the head of the household in a medieval hall; a garret room.
